summary.headline: Enviro Infra Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 60% YoY to INR363.8 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 20.58% from 28.56%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 60% YoY to INR363.8 crore in Q2 FY27, while consolidated EBITDA excluding other income rose 15.3% to INR74.9 crore and margin compressed to 20.58%. PAT fell to INR39.5 crore from INR49.5 crore, which management attributed to input cost inflation from the West Asia conflict, higher finance and depreciation costs, interest accrued on the Suyog Urja acquisition payment, and reversal of EPC profits on group IPP projects. Management reiterated FY27 sales guidance of INR2,000 crore and a consolidated EBITDA margin of about 19-20%, with renewable EPC execution expected to ramp in Q3 and Q4. Debt rose to INR703.9 crore and receivables to INR321.8 crore, and management now expects OCF to turn positive only from Q4.

segments.name: Water and wastewater (EPC/HAM/O&M)
segments.commentary: EPC order book about INR2,106 crore, HAM INR346 crore, long-term O&M INR987 crore; guided EBITDA margin about 21%. Two new Namami Gange HAM projects in Varanasi total about INR257 crore excl. GST, taking HAM portfolio to five projects. Cumulative 58 projects, 1,018 MLD built.

segments.name: Renewable energy
segments.commentary: Renewables were about 29% of H1 FY27 consolidated revenue. Order book about INR3,340 crore: BESS INR1,100 crore, wind INR1,054 crore, solar INR111 crore, IPP INR956 crore, maintenance INR109 crore. Suyog Urja wind EPC LoIs total about INR418 crore (Parli 180 MW INR190 crore; Ajani 100 MW INR228 crore). Guided EBITDA margin 15-18%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated sales guidance of INR2,000 crore maintained; H1 delivered about INR700-723 crore, implying about INR1,300 crore in H2.
FY27 PAT expected at about INR240-250 crore.
Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at about 19-20%; water and wastewater about 21%, renewables 15-18%.
FY27 water and wastewater order inflow guidance of INR2,500 crore; about INR250 crore won so far, with INR2,250 crore still targeted in FY27.
OCF expected to turn positive from Q4 FY27.
Debt-to-equity expected at no more than 0.6 at FY27 close; UBR to be nil by March 2027 per management, with overall UBR value around INR600 crore.
O&M revenue expected to stay at about 3-4% of standalone revenue, possibly rising to about 5%.
capex_capacity: BESS EPC: about 930 MWh order from NTPC, plus one acquired Bihar IPP project; a major part expected complete by June 2026 per management.
Suyog Urja wind EPC: 180 MW Parli project due for completion by March 2027; 100 MW Ajani project in Latur LoI received October 2026.
HAM: Mathura construction complete with COD expected soon; Saharanpur in fourth milestone; Yamuna Nagar and Amritsar near completion.
Two Bangalore projects (about INR220 crore total) now under execution after earlier delay; management expects completion ahead of schedule.
Suyog Urja acquisition valued at INR311 crore: INR111 crore paid, INR200 crore due over the next two years.
demand_pricing: Diversified order book about INR6,778 crore: INR3,439 crore water and wastewater, INR3,340 crore renewables.

Competition has increased over the past five to six months; management says it is not lowering bid profitability guidance and is selective, focusing on ZLD, reuse and single-ticket wastewater projects.
Input costs rose due to the West Asia conflict; price escalation clauses in contracts do not fully pass through.
Namami Gange fund flow is not a constraint (HAM escrow funded; EPC working capital about 60 days); AMRUT funding is state-specific and working capital is more stretched.
Pipeline cited in Delhi HAM, UP ETPs, Jharkhand, Bihar, MP, Karnataka, Urban Challenge Fund, and one or two overseas bids.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 800-900 bps YoY margin decline, and what is the INR178 crore 'other construction and operating expenses' line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited West Asia-driven input cost inflation, plus accounting entries: interest on the deferred Suyog Urja payment and reversal of EPC profits on group IPP projects. It described the line as direct costs (manpower, civil labour, job works, purchases) and suggested reading it together with purchase cost; no further breakdown was given.

qa_highlights.question: What consolidated margin should be expected going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated EBITDA margin of about 19-20%, with water at about 21% and renewables at 15-18%. Renewable profitability is expected to rise in Q3 and Q4 as BESS and wind EPC scale up.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance intact and how will H2 revenue be delivered?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales guidance of INR2,000 crore and PAT of INR240-250 crore are maintained; H1 delivered about INR700 crore and the balance is to come in Q3 and Q4 from the existing order book.

qa_highlights.question: When will OCF turn positive and why is it negative?
qa_highlights.answer: OCF is expected positive from Q4 FY27. H1 was hit by about INR57 crore rise in service concession receivables (over 15 years) and trade payable days falling from 93 to 63 (about INR102 crore outgo).

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak debt level and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt-to-equity is about 0.53 now and should close FY27 at no more than 0.6. Term loans will rise moderately for HAM and IPP projects; short-term WC lines are expected to fall as cash cycles ease.

qa_highlights.question: Will the water share of the order book decline as renewables grow?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management says the water business is the core with 35 years of history. It is bidding selectively, not lowering profitability guidance, and is comfortable waiting for quality orders given the current book.

risks_watch: Margin compression: consolidated EBITDA margin 20.58% vs 28.56% a year ago; guided 19-20% for the year, with renewable margins at 15-18%.
Working capital and leverage: receivables up to INR321.8 crore from INR155.3 crore; borrowings up to INR703.9 crore; OCF negative in H1 with positive OCF targeted only from Q4.
H2 revenue ramp needed: about INR1,300 crore in Q3 and Q4 to hit INR2,000 crore; renewable EPC execution must accelerate.
Order inflow gap: INR2,250 crore of the INR2,500 crore water guidance still to be won in FY27, amid rising competition.
Input cost inflation from the West Asia conflict, with only partial pass-through.
Disclosure: management declined to break down the INR178 crore other construction and operating expense line in detail.
summary.management_tone: Confident on execution, guidance and order book, but defensive on margins and cash flow: management attributed the margin fall to accounting entries and input costs rather than operations. Answers on the INR178 crore cost line and OCF timing were vague or repetitive.
key_quotes: We are not interested in lowering the profitability guidance.
We maintain our guidance. There is no change.
There has been an implication of some interest costs which has been taken as an expense.
We expect that Q4 onwards, we should be OCF positive.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: Water order inflow gap vs INR2,500 crore target
rows.why: About INR250 crore won so far against INR2,250 crore still targeted for FY27, amid competition rising over the past 5-6 months.

rows.label: OCF turns positive from Q4 FY27

rows.label: Debt-to-equity capped at 0.6 at FY27 close
rows.why: Debt-to-equity is about 0.53 with borrowings at INR703.9 crore vs INR422.3 crore at FY26 end; management expects it not above 0.6 despite moderate term loan rise for HAM and IPP.
